obligations.note: The change uses the existing EDIT_CASE action via authorize(); no new role or action is introduced and the access matrix is untouched. The exhaustive control test matrixEqualsApprovedPolicy passes in CI.
Auditor permissions are unchanged; the new reopen method requires EDIT_CASE which the AUDITOR role does not hold. The exhaustive control test auditorIsReadOnly passes.
The ADMIN role has no EDIT_CASE grant, so it cannot call reopen. The exhaustive control test adminCannotApproveCredit passes and the matrix is unchanged.
No new HTTP route is added; the reopen method is a service-layer operation invoked through existing routes. The exhaustive route control test passes.
No session-handling code is touched; the privileged idle timeout remains at 15 minutes per policy-params.json. The exhaustive control test passes.
The change does not introduce or alter any NPI field or persistence path. The exhaustive control test everyNpiFieldIsSealedAtRest passes.
The new log line 'Case <caseId> reopened by <userId>' contains only a case identifier (e.g. HW-000042) and a user ID, neither of which is NPI. No unmasked NPI value reaches the log.

The new reopen() method changes case status from WITHDRAWN to DRAFT and persists via store.save(), making it a state-changing operation, yet it never calls audit.record(). Every other state-changing method in CaseService (withdraw, close, create, edit, etc.) records an audit event; reopen does not. This violates the obligation that every state-changing operation records an audit event with actor, action, target, and time.
The audit trail infrastructure (AuditLog, AuditEvent, chain logic) is not modified. The exhaustive chainAndRetention control test passes in CI.

Reopening a case to DRAFT simply removes it from the withdrawn set; the Retention.java logic (unchanged) only purges declined/withdrawn cases, so a reopened case is correctly retained. The sampled control test passes.
The reopen method does not approve or decline credit; it only reverts status to DRAFT. Approvals.java is unchanged and the exhaustive maker-checker control test passes.
No approval-authority logic is modified; the exhaustive control test and the proof record remain valid as the covered code is unchanged.
Underwriting.java and Policy.java are untouched; the exhaustive auto-approve grid test passes and the proof record is unaffected by this change.

summary: The change adds a reopen() method to CaseService that transitions a WITHDRAWN case back to DRAFT, authorizing the caller via EDIT_CASE. While the access-matrix, logging, and process controls (ticket, independent approval, CI) are all satisfied, the method is a state-changing operation that omits the mandatory audit.record() call that every other state-changing method in the file makes. This violates AUD-1, which requires every state-changing operation to record an audit event with actor, action, target, and time. Because a critical obligation is refuted, the change must be rejected. The author should add an audit.record() call (e.g., audit.record(actor, Action.EDIT_CASE, caseId, "reopened")) and resubmit.
